posts.author: youralphamom
posts.text:
FIFA World Cup AI Video Test.

Seedance 2.0 vs Gemini Omni Flash vs Kling 3.0 vs Grok Imagine.

My new battle for the best AI video generator.

The World Cup is starting, so I wanted to test something football-related this time.

The scene was not easy:

A player had to break through the defense, dribble past opponents, score a beautiful goal, and celebrate naturally.

Each model got around 3–8 attempts to show its best result.

Surprisingly, almost every model managed to produce something decent this time.

Except Veo 3.1, which I left out again because the quality was still too weak for this kind of test.

My take:

- Kling 3.0 did better than I expected. It needed more attempts to get a usable result, and it is still clearly behind Seedance and Gemini Omni Flash. But for such a complex sports scene, Kling looked like a solid mid-tier model.

- Gemini Omni Flash also needed a lot of attempts. It gave me great sound, nice visuals, and some very strong camera angles, but almost every generation had logic issues. The final result looks good, but the lower FPS is a noticeable weakness in this test. Good model, but still very far from a revolution.

- Grok Imagine was tested through the official Grok website again, the same way most users would. I did not use the new Grok Imagine 1.5 because it still seems to be API-only and is not available in the tools I currently use. So this is the public Grok website version. As expected, it gave the weakest result here. It lost to Kling and was far behind Gemini Omni Flash and Seedance. The physics and visual mistakes were the most obvious.

- Seedance 2.0 was excellent. It only took 3 attempts to get this result, and the first two were already decent too. Faster FPS, more logical movement, better football energy, and a much stronger celebration sequence. In a difficult sports test like this, Seedance showed again why it is still the king.

My ranking for this test:

1. Seedance 2.0 — amazing result.
2. Gemini Omni Flash — good, but still chasing when the scene requires complex action.
3. Kling 3.0 — solid mid-tier result.
4. Grok Imagine — weak again. I’m still waiting until I can properly test the newest version.

Enjoy the test.

And if you’re watching the World Cup too, enjoy the games.

Let me know your ranking.

#AIVideo

posts.author: fomoliver
posts.text:
You take a video of a dancing woman and swap her for a witch with a prompt. This already works. One tool does it like a Netflix poster, the other like homework.

Tested Gemini Omni against Seedance 2.0 on four tasks. Add fire to a video, change the character, edit a scene, turn a pencil storyboard into a finished video.

Started with fire. Woman in a white bodysuit, black cape in the wind, blue sky. Gemini put a flame vertically on her head — like a birthday candle. Seedance sent fire flowing from her hair back along the cape. Looks like she's actually burning. Burning beautifully.

Then the witch. Same dancing woman in the mountains, swapped for an old hag in a brown robe. Gemini: witch stands there, mountains stand there, everything just stands there. Seedance added fog, a low camera angle, and honestly it's unclear why Netflix still hires set designers.

Video Editing. White dress, grey backdrop, woman moving. Gemini's skirt at the bottom looks like cardboard. Seedance: the fabric lives - expands, flows, behaves like actual fabric.

Storyboard to Video. Six rough pencil panels: shoes, cologne, a watch, a guy in a suit. Gemini made a decent video. Seedance made a perfume ad you actually want to watch till the end.

Three tasks out of four. Seedance gets the medal.

Google invested $75 billion in AI in 2025. Apparently not in the right budget line.

Second independent test in a row. Same result.

posts.author: youralphamom
posts.text:
Kling 3.0 vs Gemini Omni Flash vs Grok Imagine 1.5 vs Seedance 2.0. 

Another battle for the best AI video tool.

This time I tested an extremely difficult stunt scene: a bridge jump, landing on a moving truck, then jumping onto a car and taking it over.

No model handled it perfectly.

Not even Seedance 2.0.

The scene itself was very hard, but I kept the prompt relatively simple, without stuffing it with too many complex stunt terms.

After Veo 3.1’s terrible results in previous rounds, I didn’t even include it this time.

Seedance needed 4 attempts to give me a decent result.

Gemini Omni Flash needed even more: 7 generations, and I picked the best one.

Kling and Grok got 4 attempts each. None of them looked promising enough to justify more retries.

My take:

Grok Imagine 1.5, the new “revolutionary” release, once again showed that it still can’t handle complex action scenes properly. Two tests in a row now, and the result is objectively weak.

Kling 3.0 feels outdated, but in this test it actually looked slightly better than Grok Imagine 1.5, which says a lot.

Gemini Omni Flash gives decent movement, but the physics and action logic are clearly off. It’s better than Grok and Kling here, but still very far from the super-generator Google markets it as.

Seedance 2.0 was the best again, as expected. Still not perfect. It also has a clear physics issue, because pulling a driver out of a moving car while standing on the road makes no physical sense.

But overall, Seedance still produced a much more intense and cinematic scene than all the others.

My ranking for this test:

1. Seedance 2.0 — clear winner, even with flaws
2. Gemini Omni Flash
3. Kling 3.0
4. Grok Imagine 1.5 — unfortunately, the weakest right now in my opinion

Do you agree?

#AIVideo

posts.author: codebypoonam
posts.text:
1. Image to Video in multiple styles
Upload a photo. describe the style. Gemini Omni turns it into a video. cinematic, anime, realistic.

2. Reimagine camera angles
Take any image and visualize it from a completely different angle. no reshooting. just describe it.

3. Change backgrounds
Swap the background of any video through plain conversation. no green screen. no editing software.

4. Change hairstyle
Describe a new hairstyle. Gemini Omni applies it. characters stay consistent across every frame.

5. visualize with moodboards
feed it a moodboard, audio, and a brief. it builds the video around the full creative reference — not just a text prompt.

6. swap characters and objects mid-scene
replace people, props, and objects in an existing video. the scene stays consistent. the physics hold up.

7. edit physics
describe how you want things to move. Gemini Omni adjusts the physics of the scene through conversation.

posts.author: nyaiibubu
posts.text:
Gini banget yak ? 🫢 

with Gemini Omni Flash  

Prompt The camera launches from rooftop altitude above Jakarta night skyline in pure FPV first-person point-of-view. No drone visible. No cat visible yet. The camera nose-dives full speed between skyscrapers, buildings rushing past both sides, neon signs motion-blurring. The camera barrel rolls 360 degrees mid-air revealing Bundaran HI intersection far below motorcycles, cars, wet asphalt neon reflections. The camera snaps direction violently and accelerates full throttle toward the Plaza Indonesia curved billboard. The billboard rushes toward the camera filling the entire frame.
The billboard screen displays video footage of a tuxedo cat standing on all fours in natural cat posture. Both hind legs fully covered from hip joint to paws in bright pink fabric printed with red hearts  large fitted cat pants covering entire lower half of cat body. The cat twerks aggressively on screen  rear end shaking hard left and right, pink-legging-covered hind legs stomping and bouncing, face turned 3/4 toward camera, mouth open. The camera brakes and hovers inches from billboard surface. The camera whips tight orbit around the cat face on screen then locks center.
The tuxedo cat exists ONLY as video playing inside the billboard screen. The cat is fully contained within the LED screen boundaries at all times. No part of the cat extends beyond the billboard frame. There is no cat anywhere in the scene outside the billboard screen.
Camera: Pure POV FPV rooftop altitude → full speed nose-dive between skyscrapers → 360 barrel roll → violent direction snap → full throttle billboard approach → brake hover inches from screen → tight orbit → center lock
Style: Jakarta night neon, extreme motion blur on buildings during dive, sharp focus snap onto billboard on arrival, LED screen light blasting into camera lens, lens flare on approach, GoPro FPV color grade, high contrast night, wet asphalt reflections during barrel roll
Constraints: No drone visible ever. No cat visible until billboard appears. No cat body part outside billboard frame at any point. Cat fully natural four-legged feline anatomy. Pink heart leggings fully cover BOTH hind legs from hip to paws  full coverage, not small accessories. Black nose spot sharp and consistent. Cat face AND legging-covered rear simultaneously visible in 3/4 angle. No ghosting, no flickering on LED screen, sharp fur detail, natural colors

posts.author: trendyvers
youralphamom
posts.text:
Veo 3.1 vs Gemini Omni Flash vs Grok Imagine 1.5 vs Seedance 2.0 — a new battle for the best AI video generator.

I tested all 4 models with the same difficult action prompt.

Quick note: this was not a strict one-shot test. The prompt was complex, so I gave each model up to 4 attempts max.

Here’s what happened:

Veo 3.1 — weak result, which was honestly expected at this point.

Gemini Omni Flash — surprisingly decent, but only on the 4th attempt.

Grok Imagine 1.5 — the new hyped release looked pretty weak here. On the 4th attempt, it finally beat Veo, but it was still far behind Seedance 2.0 and Gemini Omni Flash on this task.

Seedance 2.0 — nailed it on the 1st attempt. I tried a second generation too, but the first one was better. Best physics, best tension, best overall action feel.

My current ranking:

1. Seedance 2.0 — still the leader
2. Gemini Omni Flash
3. Grok Imagine 1.5
4. Veo 3.1 — feels outdated now

For this kind of complex action scene, Seedance is still clearly ahead in my opinion.

What do you think? Which model won this round?

#AIVideo

Just a simple experiment using Gemini Omni Flash for editing through the Gemini app. I included the instructions right in the middle of the video.

At first glance, the model captures intent really well regardless of how you phrase things. The first few seconds are smooth; character movement is identical, and the glowing orb tracks and circles me perfectly. It only starts to struggle once the transitions kick in.

I added some simple logic in the third clip hoping to smooth out the door transitions. Despite the flaws, the editing capabilities are solid. It really gets the intent, and both character and camera movements stay on point.

Also, Gemini changed the aspect ratio but kept the framing the same. 👀

posts.author: mrdasonx
posts.text:
The war is over. The flowers know it.

Google Gemini Omni prompt: A weary medieval knight in full shining plate armor rests peacefully under a large ancient oak tree in a vast, endless field of vibrant blooming red poppies swaying gently in the breeze. The knight lies on the soft grass, helmet still on, eyes closed in serene rest, surrounded by bright red flowers. The camera starts with a wide establishing shot, then slowly dollies in with a gentle push toward the knight, maintaining shallow depth of field that keeps sharp focus on the knight and nearby poppies while softly blurring the distant field and sky. Above, dramatic stormy dark clouds fill the sky but part dramatically to let soft golden sunlight rays break through, casting beautiful god rays and dynamic natural lighting with soft shadows. The atmosphere is peaceful yet epic, evoking calm after a hard battle. Ultra-realistic cinematic fantasy style, hyper-detailed textures on armor, flowers, and grass, painterly epic mood, natural light scattering, subtle wind movement in flowers and tree leaves.
